items.anchor: comparison geometry also yields local convergence for planar smooth maxima
items.note: True as phrased under the rule for summaries: the sentence cites Corollary art:planar-max and signals its assumptions ("under strict-contour and active-gradient nondegeneracy assumptions"); the witness F(u,v)=|v| of A/introduction/prose/036 violates the strict-contour assumption. Left implicit: F finite and convex with a unique minimizer x_* (the nondegeneracy is stated at x_*); near x_*, F = max_i f_i with convex C^2 branches ("planar smooth maxima"); "strict-contour": sufficiently low positive sublevels have no nontrivial boundary segment; "active-gradient nondegeneracy": the active gradients at x_* are affinely independent with weights lambda_i^*>0, sum 1, and sum lambda_i^* grad f_i(x_*)=0; "local convergence": some eps>0, independent of H_0 and of the line-search constants, such that every infinite admissible run with F(x_0)<F_*+eps has F(x_k)->F_* and x_k->x_*.

items.anchor: Neither a bounded condition
Our conditions are sufficient; they do not classify every successful run.
items.note: Reading: the second clause asserts non-necessity. "They do not classify every successful run" denies that every successful run falls under the sufficient conditions, i.e. some successful BFGS behavior satisfies none of them; the first clause only restates that the positive results are implications. This is the claim of energy.tex:311-311, covered in Lean by A/energy/prose/035 (certificate_not_necessary: an objective on which every admissible run converges while no sublevel admits band certificates; the radial, centered, homogeneous and polyhedral criteria all act through band certificates, and the planar criteria concern n=2). Theorem art:nonradial-example also shows that the radial condition alone is not necessary.
